headline: Google ad imagines Founding Fathers using Google Workspace
summary: New commercial sparks outrage with AI-powered collaboration tools
details: The commercial, meant to showcase Google Workspace, depicts the founding fathers using the platform to draft the Declaration of Independence. The ad features Benjamin Franklin, Thomas Jefferson, and John Adams using Google's collaboration tools and Gemini AI.

The ad shows the founding fathers using Google Docs, Google Meet, and other tools to collaborate on the document. The ad also features a meeting with King George III, which has sparked outrage and criticism.

Critics have panned the ad as 'ill-advised, corny, and just plain dumb.' CUNY history professor Angus Johnston stated that 'even in a corny fantasy joke, it's impossible to make the case that AI is a useful tool for political organizing, writing, or human collaboration.'

headline_marked: US Navy flight-tests [[3D printed F/A-18 parts]] to cut repair times in half
headline: US Navy flight-tests 3D printed F/A-18 parts to cut repair times in half
summary: The US Navy is testing 3D printed fighter jet parts to reduce repair times. This method could improve operational readiness.
details: The US Navy is flight-testing 3D printed parts for F/A-18 Super Hornets to reduce repair times. This method allows for on-site 3D printing of composite parts at forward operating bases.

The 3D printing technique enables troops to print composite patches and apply them directly to the aircraft, reducing reliance on lengthy logistics chains. This approach cuts repair times by around 50%.
Laboratory and ground tests have proven the viability of these 3D printed repairs. The next step is to assess their performance under real-world operational stresses.
Other military branches are also exploring 3D printing to streamline operations and logistics. This includes 3D printing drones and other equipment in the field.
